name: Albania
headline: Albania: +3.7% growth in 2025, 2.2% inflation, debt 54% of GDP
sections: Albania is a $30.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 118th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.7% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $28K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 6.0% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.2% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 6.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 8.7% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 25.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 54% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 75% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.8% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −0.7% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 80% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 6.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 46% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 79.8 years (2024). Population: 2.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
